vision:
OpenAxolotl is a joyful single-player adventure game where families explore and restore imaginative worlds, then create adventures of their own together. A shared library of polished characters, environments and mechanics helps turn their ideas into playable levels. Reviewed community adventures become new destinations for everyone to explore.

THE GAME COMES FIRST. Children should enjoy the shipped game without creating anything or needing an AI account. Our axolotl's expressive movement, land-and-water traversal, readable robot encounters, discoveries and restoration rewards create the sense of adventure. Astro Bot inspires pacing, clarity and responsiveness; matching another game's production quality is an aspiration, not an unmeasured acceptance claim.

PLAY, CREATE, SHARE. Play official adventures. With a parent, remix a small playable starter using the shared asset/gameplay kit, Codex and NodeSpec, previewing and iterating in Godot. Direct Godot editing remains supported. Submit a level for automated checks and human review; approved, versioned adventures can be downloaded and played through the hub. Creation is optional, parent-led for young children, and separate from the child-facing game.

FOUR RESPONSIBILITIES. Core game systems own the hero, movement, camera, combat, regeneration/capabilities, checkpoints, saves, restoration, collectibles, audio and common enemy behaviors. A reusable Level Kit packages approved assets with materials, collision and supported gameplay behavior. Individual levels own layout, placements, objectives and presentation configuration. Authoring and distribution own the starter workflow, export/validation, review, curated catalog and package lifecycle. Levels use a small versioned public World API; shared code contains no hardcoded coordinates for a particular world.

CONTENT EXTENSIONS. Local authoring may use code and Godot scenes. Published downloadable level packages contain only supported declarative content and approved component/asset references. Arbitrary scripts, native extensions and executable scene resources are excluded from that package format. New powers or enemy logic that require executable changes are separately reviewed core contributions. The package schema and loader must be designed and tested; this is a target architecture, not a claim that the current repository already implements it.

FIRST ADVENTURE REFERENCE. Open Lagoon is the safe starting cove. Its leftmost downstream tunnel connects to Coral Cove, currently presented as The Living Cascade: Arrival Pool; Stepping-stone Garden; Hollow-root Dive; Cascade Terraces; Restoration Garden; Waterfall Run; completion and return to the hub. The current finish uses a reach_volume trigger, not a mandatory boss. Preserve three checkpoints, optional discoveries, glowing crayfish and the optional dance reward. Three Netbots occupy land; five Hooklines are distributed across land and underwater positions. The restoration gate requires seven total seeds, with nine available and seven accessible within the garden alone. Accessible shores, entrance seams and underwater/pool boundaries are contained; accidental fallthrough is a defect. A whirlpool, additional suit powers and a new boss remain future work until separately specified.

DELIVERY. Desktop is the first release target. Tablet play is a later feasibility milestone requiring measured performance, touch controls and readable UI on named devices; it is not promised by the current art quality. Consoles are deferred. This remains a single-player game, not a general-purpose engine or a multiplayer platform.

OPEN CONTRIBUTION. Establish code licensing, asset remix/redistribution rights, provenance, credits and contributor permissions before inviting public reuse. The repository's code license does not automatically cover externally generated models, textures or music. Publish only packages that pass conformance checks, human play/content review and measured device budgets. Approval identifies immutable package bytes; updates are reviewed again and withdrawn releases are removed from future distribution.

This new project records the agreed end state and the first-level reference. Existing implementation is context only: no requirement is considered verified until fresh evidence is attached after the repository is connected. Do not overwrite this specification with older repository anchors during connection.

requirements.name: A complete single-player adventure before creation
requirements.description: Children can enjoy the shipped official adventure independently of the optional creator ecosystem. Parent-led creation extends a finished game rather than being required to make it playable.
acceptanceCriteria: The shipped build starts and completes an official adventure without an AI account, creator tooling or a network connection.
The game contains no multiplayer dependency; optional catalog failures do not prevent playing installed official content.
A recorded family playtest evaluates the clarity and enjoyment of the official start-to-finish route; findings are resolved or explicitly tracked.

requirements.name: Expressive, smooth axolotl movement and animation
requirements.description: Retain the character's distinct land and water movement, responsive transitions and readable actions. Polish is measured through motion continuity and play review rather than a claim of parity with Astro Bot.
acceptanceCriteria: Land/water transitions retain the configured momentum, keep collision and visual pose aligned, and do not leave the player in the wrong movement grammar.
Movement and facing accelerate and decelerate continuously at 30, 60 and 120 Hz; a swimming reversal turns through a bounded arc instead of snapping.
Swimming folds the feet toward the body with a traveling body/tail wave; underwater idle preserves gentle foot motion; tail whack visibly reaches forward and has a bounded hit window.

Review walking, hopping, climbing, swimming, turning, tail whack and spin charge in the production camera; underwater spin bubbles/current and land-slide surface disturbance communicate the action without obscuring threats.
The character has exactly one authoritative physics-root writer; animation, backpack and surface effects cannot change the collision root, damage reach or movement velocity.

At a fixed 60 Hz physics step, the same timed input replay rendered at 30, 60 and 120 FPS finishes within 5 percent of reference travel distance and 5 degrees of reference heading, with identical action and checkpoint events.
Allowed locomotion inputs affect simulation within two physics ticks; buffered jump and interruption windows are configurable and tests cover their boundary ticks.

A versioned animation transition table covers idle, start, travel, turn, stop, jump, fall, land, swim, surface, dive, attack, capture, dance and reset; every allowed edge exits without a stuck pose, duplicate action event or stale blend.

Audit and approve the production rig, skin weights, clip coverage and contact chains; document whether each limb supports planted-foot solving and replace the current one-joint limb limitation before promising full foot locking.

Approve a fixed production-camera reel at normal speed and slow motion covering starts, stops, reversals, slopes, landing, swimming transitions and moving attacks; resolve visible foot sliding, snapping, broken deformation and mechanical body/tail motion before declaring the character-polish milestone complete.

requirements.name: Readable camera, controls and accessible feedback
requirements.description: Support keyboard/mouse and gamepad on desktop with clear camera framing, input prompts and multiple feedback channels.
acceptanceCriteria: Every mandatory action is available on keyboard/mouse and gamepad; remapped inputs update the prompts.
The follow camera handles terrain obstruction and underwater passages without clipping through blocking geometry or losing the player.
Mandatory routes, enemy warnings and restoration changes remain understandable without relying only on color or audio; music/effects volume and reduced-motion options are reviewed.

Input is sampled independently of presentation, normalized to semantic actions and consumed once per physics tick; dead zones, remapping and focus loss cannot create repeated presses or stuck movement.

Camera collision and framing use the same reference traversal through the inlet, root tunnel and terrace edges; changing render FPS cannot create a one-frame camera teleport except an explicit respawn cut.
Approve controller feel and camera framing in the same character reel, including a reduced-motion profile, before expanding world dressing.

requirements.name: Nearby enemies with readable, smooth behavior
requirements.description: Netbots occupy land; Hooklines support land and underwater habitats. Encounters use perception, bounded patrols, telegraphs, committed attacks and readable recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: An enemy acquires the player only inside its authored awareness range and valid line of sight, respects its home leash and habitat, and returns smoothly when pursuit ends.
Attack wind-up, active contact and recovery are distinct; committed attacks do not rotate or home after release and cancelled attacks cannot retain active hit windows.
A valid strike defeats an ordinary robot once per action, produces bounded mechanical debris, disables its attack/collision as appropriate, and cleans up debris.
Production encounters are reviewed for smooth acceleration, turning and pose transitions, readable timing and space to evade.

Enemy acceleration, heading and pose transitions use versioned habitat-specific tuning and pass the same timed pursuit/return replay at 30, 60 and 120 render FPS without different attack counts or out-of-habitat motion.

requirements.name: Netbot capture and Hookline attack rules
requirements.description: Keep the currently requested opponent identities and escape rules, with optional encounters that do not silently become progression gates.
acceptanceCriteria: Netbot uses the animated net contact socket; three distinct tail-whack presses strictly before two seconds escape capture, while timeout resets to the active checkpoint without an additional life penalty.
Escaping a net clears the capture state but does not automatically defeat Netbot; a later valid attack can defeat it.
Hookline throws toward the committed player position and retracts over three seconds without homing or new recovery hits; any equipped-Gill-Mod snag uses the bounded existing timer.
A player without a Gill Mod can evade or defeat Hookline and can complete the first adventure.

Net capture, escape, death and checkpoint reset cancel all outstanding attack tokens and contact windows; a held button counts as one press, and an escape input at or after the two-second deadline fails.

requirements.name: Glowing crayfish and an optional dance reward
requirements.description: Blue shore and underwater pickups are recognizable animated crayfish. Their reward adds personality without blocking adventure progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Crayfish move within authored shore or underwater habitats with their pickup trigger aligned to the visible creature; they cannot escape into inaccessible terrain.
Collecting five unique glowing crayfish unlocks a reusable dance; repeated collection of the same identity cannot increase the saved total.
Dance starts only on a flat, clear shore while stationary; movement, water entry, damage, capture or checkpoint reset cancels it. It grants no invulnerability and consumes no collected crayfish.
The hero stands on hind legs for the line-dance-inspired routine with a separate groove cue; ordinary background music remains unobtrusive and has independent volume control.

requirements.name: Consistent recovery, capabilities and saved progress
requirements.description: Preserve existing regeneration/capability, lives/checkpoint and Gill Mod concepts behind explicit public interfaces. Unexpected fallthrough is a defect, not an intended difficulty mechanic.
acceptanceCriteria: Checkpoint activation and respawn restore position, velocity and the documented capability/life snapshot without leaving attack, capture or dance states active.
Restoration, completion, unique discoveries and dance unlock persist through save/reload under documented namespaces.
Unavailable abilities or reduced capability do not softlock the first adventure; mandatory recovery paths remain reachable.
Document exactly which encounters can remove capability or consume a life; neither the future whirlpool nor future suit powers are treated as implemented requirements.

requirements.name: Four architectural responsibilities and a versioned World API
requirements.description: Separate core runtime, reusable Level Kit, world content and authoring/distribution. Reuse the working Godot systems incrementally; do not rewrite the engine. API and package schemas must be concrete before code is built against them.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared runtime modules contain no world-specific placement coordinates or world-owned spawn lists; each world owns its layout, objectives and placements.
Levels access checkpoint, collectible, restoration, encounter and completion services only through the documented versioned public World API; static checks reject private cross-boundary access.
The contract requires spawn, checkpoints, finish, controller/runtime compatibility and save integration, with explicit optional defaults and migration rules.
An ownership map assigns each source file to one primary component and documents cross-component contracts before implementation changes.

A single runtime composition point wires shared services; level content never writes the player physics root, imports private runtime members or registers arbitrary scripts through the downloadable content path.

Document the migration from the current script-bearing level contract and global no-network policy to separate trusted local-authoring and data-only download paths; catalog networking is isolated from world behavior and offline gameplay remains supported.

requirements.name: A reusable gameplay kit with coherent presentation
requirements.description: Give creators usable gameplay components rather than isolated meshes: terrain, water, enemies, checkpoints, pickups, gates, materials, lighting and audio with documented parameters.
acceptanceCriteria: Each catalog entry has a stable ID/version, supported parameters, required dependencies, habitat/collision rules and rights/provenance metadata.
Gameplay prefabs ship with appropriate collision, interaction volumes and bounded behavior; decorative motion cannot move gameplay collision.

Land surfaces, shores, grass, rock, underwater depth gradients, waterfall origins, hero and enemies meet the starting-lagoon visual reference at gameplay distance without stretched pixelated textures or distracting repetition.
Art and sound review checks action readability, sensible material scale, adjustable low-level background music and a distinct dance cue; asset and device budgets are recorded separately.

The kit records mesh units, pivot/forward conventions, visual bounds, gameplay hulls, material scale and animation sockets; importing a revised model fails visibly when its required rig/socket contract is incompatible.
Approve one representative shore-to-underwater section with final lighting, material blends, silhouette variety and collision before extending the same treatment across all sections.

requirements.name: A small, approachable family level-creation workflow
requirements.description: Parents and children can remix a small complete example through Codex and NodeSpec or direct Godot editing. AI is optional for playing and the direct editor path remains supported.
acceptanceCriteria: The starter plays from spawn to finish and demonstrates land, water, one enemy, checkpoint, collectible and one restoration or supported ability gate through the same public interfaces as official levels.
A documented first remix changes one bounded part of the starter and passes conformance without editing core systems.
A newcomer test covers setup, describing an idea, editing, previewing, checking and exporting; the 15–30 minute first-remix goal is measured after setup and reported honestly.
Parent-facing instructions clearly distinguish local experimentation, supported downloadable content and executable core contributions.

A family trial starts from a clean pinned-toolchain setup and records time, errors and assistance for a bounded AI-assisted remix and an equivalent direct-Godot edit; export and playtest must succeed without core changes.

requirements.name: A bounded, versioned downloadable content format
requirements.description: Local Godot source may be freely iterated, but published level packages contain only supported declarative content and approved component/asset references. A Godot scene or PCK is not assumed safe merely because it is called content.
acceptanceCriteria: The machine-readable package schema defines identity/version, contract/runtime/kit compatibility, sections, spawn, checkpoints, objectives, finish, asset references, save schema, credits and integrity metadata.
Export and load reject scripts, native extensions, executable resource/scene references, unknown behavior IDs, invalid parameter ranges and paths outside the package namespace.
A conforming starter exports and loads through the same runtime content path used for approved community levels.
A proposed mechanic requiring new executable behavior is routed to a separate reviewed core-code change rather than smuggled into a downloadable level.

Trusted editor authoring may use scripts and scenes, but export compiles supported placements into the downloadable data schema; the runtime never loads a submitted executable scene or script as content.

requirements.name: Automated content checks and reproducible builds
requirements.description: Conformance validates the level actually played, including route safety and progression, and fails with actionable diagnostics. Existing historical test results are not copied as fresh proof.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs level/schema checks, asset checks, public-API/static rules, representative real-input route tests and the relevant core regressions from a documented clean setup.
Validation detects missing markers, unreachable required progression, gate bypasses, capsule-sized containment gaps and invalid habitat placement.
Package validation enforces file-count, compressed/uncompressed size and allowed-resource limits, safe paths and integrity checks before activation.
Each acceptance criterion records a current result or an explicit manual review; skipped, stale or historical checks are not reported as passing.

Test plans use one initial binding scenario per automated acceptance criterion and a separate manual checklist; performance measurements use a rendered build and visual quality is never inferred from a headless pass.
Route tests drive the production controller with real input through entrance, pools, underwater turns and every section; teleporting between checkpoints cannot count as traversal proof.

requirements.name: Human review before community publication
requirements.description: A curated family-facing library requires both automated validation and human review of the exact submitted version. Contributors receive actionable feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Publication is blocked until required automated checks and recorded human approvals are present for the exact package digest and version.
The review checklist covers playability, recovery, clarity, content suitability, accessibility, asset rights and measured performance on the declared hardware tier.
Changing submitted bytes invalidates approval and requires a new version/review; a rejected candidate remains unavailable to the public catalog.
Credits, contributor permissions and parent-led submission instructions are understandable before submission.

requirements.name: Curated discovery and reliable package installation
requirements.description: The hub exposes official and approved community adventures. Failed or incompatible downloads must not damage the game or existing installs.
acceptanceCriteria: Only approved compatible non-withdrawn package versions appear as installable releases, with author credits and compatibility information.
Downloads are staged, verified against the approved release record and activated atomically; interruption, invalid content or failed verification preserves the previous working install.
A missing or incompatible world shows an actionable unavailable state while the hub and other installed worlds remain playable.
Official and previously installed supported content remains playable without a network connection or AI account.

Install verification checks a release signature against the bundled trusted publisher key and the package digest before activation; unsupported keys, tampering or downgrade outside the compatibility policy preserve the prior installation.

requirements.name: Compatible updates, save migrations and withdrawal
requirements.description: Treat package versioning and saves as a lifecycle. Stable world identity survives releases; incompatible migrations are not attempted silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Progress is isolated by stable world identity and save-schema version; one level cannot read or overwrite another level's save namespace.
Updates declare compatibility/migration behavior; failed migrations retain the prior installation and recoverable save data.
Removing a level preserves progress by default; irreversible progress deletion requires an explicit separate player action.
Withdrawn releases stop being offered for installation; rollback is offered only when both runtime and save-schema compatibility permit it.

requirements.name: Explicit code, asset and contributor rights
requirements.description: The open-source promise distinguishes source-code licensing from permissions for models, textures, music and submitted levels. Externally generated assets need reviewed provenance and redistribution/remix rights.
acceptanceCriteria: The exportable asset catalog excludes assets lacking a recorded approved redistribution/remix status and required attribution.
Review and publish the code license, asset reuse terms, generator/third-party obligations and contributor permissions before inviting public reuse or submissions.
Each published package retains its credited asset manifest and required attribution through installation and updates.

requirements.name: Desktop-first quality with a separate tablet decision
requirements.description: Ship a polished desktop experience first. Tablet play is a later feasibility decision; console certification and multiplayer are outside the current delivery scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Name the desktop baseline hardware and approve numerical frame-time, memory, load-time and restoration-hitch budgets before release performance sign-off.
A reproducible benchmark exercises the decorated first adventure with water, active enemies, debris and restoration and reports its measurements against the approved budgets.
A tablet release is not committed until touch controls, UI readability, memory, sustained thermal/frame-time behavior and distribution constraints are demonstrated on named devices.
Release notes distinguish tested platforms from experimental targets and do not equate a triangle ceiling with verified performance.

The initial desktop quality target is 60 FPS with p95 frame time at most 16.7 ms, p99 at most 33.3 ms and no steady-play frame above 50 ms over a five-minute rendered benchmark after a declared warm-up; world entry is measured separately against 3000 ms. Hardware, resolution, renderer, quality preset, memory budget and capture overhead must be recorded before this can pass.

Approve the character reel, representative decorated section and family-remix trial as separate quality gates; failure creates named corrective work and cannot be waived by merely passing functional tests.

requirements.name: Repository onboarding preserves this end-state specification
requirements.description: The owner will connect the existing NodeSpec/OpenAxolotl repository after project creation. Inventory and reconcile actual implementation against this new specification without replacing it with old anchors.
acceptanceCriteria: Before enabling sync or importing anchors, compare the repository's model/spec with this project and explicitly choose the authoritative documents; retain the old project as history.
Repository files are mapped to their responsible nodes with traceable paths and commit references; generated anchors are not misbound as component source.
Requirements remain unverified until fresh automated evidence or recorded manual approval is attached; old test ticks are not imported as current proof.
Track implementation gaps separately from desired behavior, including content export/loader, curated distribution, future suit powers, whirlpool and boss placement.
Before code changes, record a source inventory, baseline input replays and rendered captures, open defects and migration ownership; existing historical test reports are reference material only.

requirements.name: Open Lagoon and the leftmost tunnel
requirements.description: Safe onboarding hub with walking, hopping, swimming and diving. The leftmost downstream tunnel is the continuous entrance to Coral Cove / Living Cascade.
acceptanceCriteria: The leftmost tunnel enters the Living Cascade arrival area using the correct production transform and supports the intended return path.
Hub and inlet collision contain the shipped player capsule with no unsupported entrance strips; accidental escape resets safely.
A new player can identify the entrance and practice the required controls before hostile encounters.

requirements.name: S01 — Arrival Pool
requirements.description: Release the player from the inlet, frame the distant crown and establish safe-water recovery. No enemy or mandatory jump gates this section.
acceptanceCriteria: The inlet current tapers to a stop before the pool and CP_01 activates on its reachable dry pad.
Two broad water exits and the bank route to S02 remain reachable without a tail; optional crayfish are not required.
The normal camera shows the next bank exit and crown destination without foliage obscuring them.

requirements.name: S02 — Stepping-stone Garden
requirements.description: Teach aimed hopping over forgiving water. Preserve the optional hermit-snail pocket and an easier swimming route.
acceptanceCriteria: The main landings and continuous banks connect S01 to S03 with capsule-sized clearance; the swimming alternative rejoins before the root dive.
Missed jumps reach recovery water and usable ramps; the optional hermit-snail spur cannot gate completion or bypass the root dive.
Two land Netbots and one land Hookline use readable proximity encounters without becoming a required enemy-clear gate.

requirements.name: S03 — Hollow-root Dive
requirements.description: The mandatory underwater root passage connects the garden to the terrace ascent; the lit lantern-shrimp grotto is optional.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual upright player capsule can dive beneath the root, negotiate the turn, reverse and resurface at the terrace ramp without sticking or leaving the water bounds.
The root and banks prevent a dry shortcut while preserving both open-water mouths and the optional grotto return.
Two underwater Hooklines respect their habitats and swim clearances; crayfish and the lantern shrimp remain optional.

requirements.name: S04 — Cascade Terraces
requirements.description: Combine hops, short swims and a modest climb in clusters A/B/C, with CP_02 and local recovery. Two terrace seeds help but are not required before entering the garden.
acceptanceCriteria: CP_02 activates on the approach, and all three clusters are traversable within the measured current controller envelope, including the continuous climb bypass.
Catch pools and ramps return the player to the relevant cluster, preserve capsule clearance and do not bypass the S05 restoration gate.
The two terrace seeds are reachable; one land Netbot, one underwater Hookline and one land Hookline have valid support/habitats.

requirements.name: S05 — Restoration Garden and crown arch
requirements.description: A calm restoration payoff at the top of the level, with CP_03, the main arch and a readable gate opening into the finale.
acceptanceCriteria: CP_03 activates on the required approach; all seven garden seeds are accessible before the finale gate opens.
Restoration spends three seeds for the first phase and four more for the second; seven total opens the gate, with nine seeds available across S04/S05.
Fresh entry with zero, one or two terrace seeds completes after seven, six or five garden seeds respectively; save/reload cannot softlock the gate.
The visible restoration and gate opening are readable from the garden pickups; no deposit station, boss or enemy-clear objective is introduced.

requirements.name: S06 — Waterfall Run and reward pool
requirements.description: Deliver a controllable descent through a banked chute beside the scenic waterfall, with a dive bar and a calm reward pool.
acceptanceCriteria: The chute is continuously contained and descending; ordinary and boosted runs can negotiate the dive bar and reach the reward pool without unbounded falls.
The dive obstacle supports stopping/reversal and active vertical control; the player is never required to swim up the waterfall.
The tide pearl and crayfish remain optional, and accidental escape uses nonlethal checkpoint recovery; no whirlpool or boss is required.

requirements.name: Finish, persist and return to Open Lagoon
requirements.description: Complete the current first adventure at its reach_volume exit and return to the hub without a mandatory boss or undefined next-world portal.
acceptanceCriteria: Crossing the designated finish volume after restoration records coral_cove.completed once and triggers the supported hub return flow.
Completion works without optional discoveries, dance unlock or defeating every enemy.
Save/reload and re-entry preserve the documented restoration/completion/discovery state and do not leave the player captured, dancing or carrying stale velocity.
